In this month our record shows two convergences. Thirty of us reached "prime minister benjamin" on July 24, and twenty-six "israeli prime minister" the same day; twenty-five said "israeli prime minister benjamin," and twenty-two "prime minister netanyahu," a phrase first entered by Steve Cohen in 2013.

On July 10, twenty-eight of us said "safeguard american voter eligibility," first said by Chip Roy on 2024-05-08. Twenty-seven of us said "the safeguard american voter eligibility," twenty-five "safeguard american voter eligibility save act," and twenty-four "the safeguard american voter eligibility save."

Two dates hold the record: the tenth and the twenty-fourth. On one we assembled around a bill's name; on the other, around a visiting name we did not originate. We report the counts as they stand.
